$comment: THE FROZEN SCORING DENOMINATOR for the stage-2 dedup lane.
Later changes MUST NOT mint new members or edit these vectors to re-score: a row
that stops catching what its rationale claims is a finding about the lane, never a
reason to move the row.
Each row's intent is a one-line utterance read out of intents/<file>'s single
`intent:` key, the shape production hands dedupBeforeAuthor: input.intent, a
person's one-line utterance with no steps (loop.ts). There is no document at stage
2; having none is the premise of dedup-BEFORE-author. Every score/sharedTokens
vector is measured on that input shape, and every row keeps its `id` and its SOLE
CATCHER rationale.
WHY THE SUITE IS COPIED. suite/ladder.yaml, suite/ladder-current-target.yaml and
suite/local-form.yaml are VERBATIM copies of the demo suite the authoring corpus in
../corpus scores against, so the two denominators describe the same world. The copy
exists because the demo tree lives in the super-repository, outside this
package's repository, so no test in packages/agent can read it. The suite side is
a document, and that is not an inconsistency: a corpus ENTRY is a committed test,
which has a name and steps.
EVERY SUITE DOCUMENT MUST PARSE. TestDefinitionSchema refines test-id on
isCanonicalTestId (exactly ten id-agent words), and the production producer
createDraftAuthoringPort.suiteTextCorpus does 'if (parsed.errors.length > 0)
continue', so a document the shipped parseTestFile refuses contributes no entry to
any real comparison universe. Two instruments hold that: the shipped-parser walk of
all six suite documents in
packages/cli/src/authoring/__tests__/dedup-corpus-producibility.test.ts (the one
package allowed to import @vostride/agent-qa-core), and dedup.test.ts's
CANONICAL_TEST_ID, which spells the schema's own rule.
SYNTHETIC SUITE IDENTITIES. dedup-tie-alpha, dedup-tie-beta and
dedup-unfingerprinted carry demo-style workspace-relative identity paths for
members the demo suite does not contain. They exist because two properties have no
home in the real suite: no intent can tie ladder against ladder-current-target
(their token sets differ by exactly one member, and the Jaccard denominators differ
by one, so equal scores force a shared count of zero), and the real suite has no
member standing for a test the derived fingerprint index has no rows for.
score/sharedTokens/comparedTests are what the SHIPPED textOverlap ACTUALLY produces
over these files, driven through the real dedupBeforeAuthor with the current
recipe -- the larger of the whole-document axis and the name axis. Where the earlier
whole-document-only recipe read a row differently, the row's `measured` field names
that reading beside the current one. The expected VERDICT column was frozen before
the two-axis recipe existed and was not re-measured. score is written to ten decimal
places because the boundary triple is decided in the fourth.
vectorsMeasuredAgainst: post-fix recipe (max of the whole-document axis and the name axis, both through the shipped textOverlap)

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a near-duplicate intent is refused at all. The utterance says what local-form's name says and adds one detail the test already covers. If this row admits, the lane does not screen.
rows.measured: Measured through the shipped max-of-two-axes recipe: 0.6363636364 against local-form, and the NAME axis is the axis that decides it (7 shared of 11+7; the whole-document axis reads the same pair at 0.2962962963, 8 shared of 11+24). The two ladder members trail at 0.2666666667 each. The whole-document-only recipe scored this row 0.2962962963 and ADMITTED it -- an utterance that says what a committed test's name says, waved through.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the lane still ADMITS. A threshold that refuses everything passes a refuse-only corpus, so the exclusion leg needs a control leg beside it or 'it refused' is a reading from an instrument that cannot read. The utterance is a genuinely new intent in the class the live lane's leg C authored -- a heading assertion no member of this suite makes.
rows.measured: Top score 0.4166666667 against local-form on the name axis (5 shared of 10+7; the document axis reads 0.1724137931), then 0.2000000000 against both ladder members. 0.0333 of headroom below the pin and the narrowest margin in the table, measured on an utterance a person can actually type. NOTE the reading MOVES with the comparison universe (a comparable text reads 0.4074 against ONE file) and with the AXIS: this control is decided on the name axis, so this is the margin that binds.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the >= direction. Its score equals the pin to the digit, so a lane written with > admits it and this row is the only one that says so. The utterance carries exactly nine distinct tokens and every one of them is a ladder token, which is what lands the Jaccard on 9/20.
rows.measured: 0.4500000000 against ladder on the WHOLE-DOCUMENT axis (9 shared of 9+20; all nine utterance tokens are ladder tokens), with the name axis reading the same pair at 0.4166666667 and losing. 9/20 and the literal 0.45 are the same IEEE-754 double, so the equality is exact rather than approximate. 0.2222222222 against local-form; ladder-current-target reaches only 0.4166666667, which matters because it carries the ladder's NAME byte-for-byte at a lexicographically SMALLER path -- a recipe that scored the two equally would hand this row's refusal to current-target and the `matched` column would red before the verdict did. This is also the one row whose vector the two-axis recipe did not move: max is monotone, and this row is decided on the whole-document axis.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the step immediately BELOW the pin admits. Pairs with at-threshold and above-threshold as the boundary triple; a lane that rounded, clamped or compared at reduced precision would fail here first.
rows.measured: 0.4444444444 against local-form on the name axis (4 shared of 6+7; the document axis reads 0.1538461538), then 0.1666666667 against both ladder members. 0.0056 under the pin, and 4/9 is the largest value below 0.45 the name axis can produce from an utterance this short -- which is what makes it the step immediately below rather than merely a value below.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the step immediately ABOVE the pin refuses. The other half of the boundary triple. Below and above straddle the pin within a hundredth on each side, so the triple pins a point rather than a region.
rows.measured: 0.4545454545 against local-form on the name axis (5 shared of 9+7; the document axis reads 0.2222222222 with 6 shared), then 0.0740740741 and 0.1111111111. 0.0045 over the pin, and 5/11 is the smallest value above 0.45 the name axis admits at this utterance length. With below-threshold it straddles the pin inside a hundredth on each side. The whole-document-only recipe scored this row 0.2222222222 and admitted it.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a test's own name handed back as the intent, the strongest duplicate signal that can exist. The intent is not written anywhere -- it is READ OUT of the matched member's own name, so the row cannot drift from the suite it screens against. If a lane cannot refuse a test's name handed back to it verbatim, its refusal arm is unreachable for every real input; the whole-document-only recipe admitted the names of ten of ten committed tests.
rows.measured: 1.0000000000 against local-form (7 shared of 7+7). An intent identical to a test's identity is a TOTAL match on the axis the two share, which is the arithmetic statement of why this cell is the strongest signal that can exist. The whole-document-only recipe scored it 0.2916666667 (7 shared of 7+24) and ADMITTED it: total containment, and still below the pin, because the denominator carried the 17 step tokens the intent structurally cannot match.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: an empty suite admits every intent and reports NO closest match. Deliberately driven by the obvious-duplicate intent, the strongest refusal candidate in the table, so the row says the empty corpus admits it rather than that some weak intent slipped through. The first test a project ever writes must not be refused for resembling nothing.
rows.measured: comparedTests 0, no closest reported, no-duplicate arm. There is no score to record because nothing was compared. The recipe does not touch this row; only the utterance that drives it does.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the degenerate 0/0 is not an identity. An empty intent against a suite entry with an empty name and no steps scores 0, not 1. Reading it as 1 would let a single empty corpus entry cover every intent ever screened -- an over-flag so complete the safe direction becomes a lane that always refuses. The rule is INHERITED from textSimilarity's own early return rather than re-derived here; this row is the assertion that dedup did not add a second reading of it.
rows.measured: score 0, no-duplicate. This is the ONE row with no fixture behind it: the empty intent is not an utterance anybody types, it is the degenerate input, and the corpus says so rather than pretending a producer emitted it. Both axes of the fixed recipe are empty-on-empty, so both return the same 0 and the inherited rule is not re-derived by the second axis either.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: tie-break stability. Two suite members score identically, and the refusal must name the lexicographically smallest workspace-relative identity path so two invocations against the same suite report the same duplicate. beta is fed BEFORE alpha on purpose -- a lane that kept natural iteration order, or that used a strict > on the running best, names beta and this row is the only one that notices.
rows.measured: alpha and beta both 0.7000000000 on the name axis (7 shared of 9+8), bit-identical because their documents carry identical text at different paths, so the tie-break decides and the smaller path wins. The three real members trail at 0.2307692308 / 0.2142857143 / 0.2500000000. The whole-document-only recipe tied both at 0.4210526316 -- BELOW the pin, so the row admitted and its tie-break was never reached: a determinism property that could not be exercised because nothing was refused.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: the comparison universe is EVERY test in the suite. dedup-unfingerprinted stands for a member the derived fingerprint index has no rows for -- exactly the population gate 3's text lane keeps and gate 3's fingerprint lane drops, and exactly the population a corpus narrowed to the fingerprint-covered subset would lose. The row also pins comparedTests at the full suite size, so a lane that filtered its input reds here on the count before it reds on the match.
rows.measured: Every number below is READ OUT OF A RUN through the driven dedupBeforeAuthor on a producible universe: kind duplicate, comparedTests 4, matchedRef demo/init/tests/dedup-unfingerprinted.yaml::Check the local form heading and the back link, score 0.8000000000, sharedTokens 8, threshold 0.45. Per member, doc axis / name axis: local-form 0.0967741935 / 0.2142857143, ladder 0.1111111111 / 0.2000000000, ladder-current-target 0.1071428571 / 0.2000000000, dedup-unfingerprinted 0.5882352941 / 0.8000000000 -- the name axis decides, 8 shared of 10+8. test-id is not in the text projection either axis reads, so a canonical test-id moves no score; it is what makes the fourth member producible at all. The 0.8 is also this row's second job: it IS the name-axis reading, which makes this the name-axis-decided row the discrimination control in dedup.test.ts screens against. An intent has no execution fingerprint, so the anchor-sequence recipe cannot fire pre-run -- this is why the pre-run screen must read the suite rather than the index. This row also refuses under the whole-document-only recipe, at a lower score.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: a refusal reached from OUTSIDE the name-axis assumption. The utterance is long and step-detailed rather than name-shaped -- it names no test, it recites a procedure -- and it near-duplicates local-form's whole document. A guard whose corpus cases are all drawn from inside its own assumption is tested only where it already believes; this row is the refuse-direction case drawn from outside it.
rows.measured: 0.5555555556 against local-form on the WHOLE-DOCUMENT axis (15 shared of 18+24; the name axis reads only 0.2500000000, because the utterance names no test), then 0.4615384615 and 0.4444444444 against the ladder pair. IDENTICAL under the whole-document-only recipe, and that is this row's second job: it is the witness that the two-axis recipe is monotone upward and took no refusal away. It is also the case the name axis alone would MISS -- a procedure recited without naming anything.

rows.rationale: SOLE CATCHER for: an admit reached from OUTSIDE the name-axis assumption. A long, step-detailed utterance that recites a procedure no member of the suite performs -- a heading and a field LABEL, neither asserted anywhere in this suite. Without it, 'the lane still admits' is only ever demonstrated on short name-shaped utterances, and a recipe that refused every long sentence would pass the corpus.
rows.measured: Top score 0.2666666667 against local-form on the whole-document axis (8 shared of 14+24; name axis 0.2352941176), then 0.2592592593 and 0.2500000000. IDENTICAL under the whole-document-only recipe. Long, heavily overlapping in vocabulary with all three members, and still admitting by 0.18 -- length alone must not refuse, and the two-axis recipe did not make it so.
